result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_partial_duplication_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add a graph grown by partial node duplication from a small complete graph. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_partial_duplication_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add a graph grown by partial node duplication from a small complete graph. title: >- [Graph.add_partial_duplication_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Add a graph grown by partial node duplication from a small complete graph. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a graph grown by partial node duplication from a small complete graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L14680-L14784){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_partial_duplication_graph( n, n_initial, p, q, seed=None, type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Partial duplication graph](../assets/graphs/add-partial-duplication-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three partial duplication graphs on a ring of eight nodes, grown from a triangle on the first three nodes. Each new node copies a random node, keeps each of its edges with probability p=0.5, and links to the original with probability q=0, 0.5, and 1. With q=0 a copy that keeps no edge is left isolated, as three are here; with q=1 every copy stays attached to its original." width="100%"} Starts from a complete graph on `n_initial` nodes and adds nodes one at a time until there are `n`. Each new node picks an existing node at random and copies part of its neighborhood: it joins each of that node's neighbors independently with probability `p`, and then the node itself with probability `q`. Unlike `add_duplication_divergence_graph()`, a new node that gets no edge is kept, so the graph can have isolated nodes. The model (Chung, Lu, Dewey and Galas 2003) gives power-law degree distributions for suitable `p`, and is NetworkX's `partial_duplication_graph()` with `N=n` and `n=n_initial`. In a directed graph every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Partial duplication graphs are useful for: - modeling the evolution of biological networks by gene duplication - copying models of the web, where new pages copy part of an existing page's links - heavy-tailed test graphs with tunable density ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Final number of nodes. Must be at least `n_initial=`. [n_initial]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Size of the starting complete graph. Must be at least `1` when `n > 0`. [p]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability, between `0` and `1`, that the new node joins each neighbor of the copied node. [q]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability, between `0` and `1`, that the new node joins the copied node itself. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` or `n_initial=` is negative, `n_initial=` exceeds `n=` (or is `0` while `n > 0`), or `p=` or `q=` is outside `0` to `1`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Growing a triangle to 100 nodes: ::: {#7871de04 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_partial_duplication_graph(n=100, n_initial=3, p=0.5, q=0.5, seed=2) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (100, 370) ``` ::: ::: With `q=1` every new node is joined at least to the node it copied, so the graph stays connected: ::: {#dbf4160f .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} joined = ec.Graph().add_partial_duplication_graph(n=100, n_initial=3, p=0.5, q=1, seed=2) joined.is_connected() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` True ``` ::: :::
